draft.title: Ambiguity and multiple meanings
card: A text is ambiguous when it supports more than one reasonable meaning. A writer may do this on purpose, so that the reader has to weigh the possibilities.
Ambiguity can sit in an ending that does not say what happens, in a symbol that points to several ideas, or in a character whose motives are unclear.
A strong reading admits the ambiguity. It does not pretend the text has one fixed meaning, and it uses evidence from the text to show why more than one reading is possible.
It then argues for what the ambiguity adds, such as tension, realism or a challenge to the reader's assumptions. Ambiguity is not a flaw in the writing just because it is open.
draft.remember: Admit the open meanings, then argue for what the openness adds.

a.q: Which sentence best shows a strong reading of an ambiguous ending?
opts: The open ending leaves the reader unsure, which adds tension
The ending is confusing, so the writer failed to finish well
The ending clearly shows that the character wins in the end
The ending means nothing, so any reading is as good as any
a.why: The first option admits the ending is open and argues for what that adds. The second treats ambiguity as a flaw, which the card says it is not. The last says any reading will do, but a strong reading still uses evidence.
a.clue: Look for the option that admits the openness and says what it adds.

b.q: In a short story, a locked door is never opened. It could stand for secrets, fear or lost chances. Which response to this symbol is strongest?
opts: Argue that the meanings keep the reader uneasy, using details
Pick one meaning and say the other meanings are simply wrong
Say the symbol is poorly chosen because it is unclear
List the three meanings but give no evidence or argument
b.why: The strongest response admits the several meanings and argues, with evidence, for what they add. Choosing one meaning ignores the ambiguity. Merely listing meanings is weaker, because it does not argue for what the ambiguity adds.
b.clue: A strong reading needs both evidence and an argument about the effect.
